newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore to allow more mobile phone firms in 2000.
newsitem.headline: Singapore to allow more mobile phone firms in 2000.

text.p: In a further liberalisation of its mobile telephone services market, Singapore said on Wednesday it would call for tenders later this year to award one or two more licences from 2000.

"The Telecommunications Authority of Singapore (TAS) will be calling for tenders later this year to award up to two more cellular licences for provision of services from April 2000," Minister for Communications Mah Bow Tan said in a speech to a business group.
The number of licences awarded would depend on the quality and attractiveness of the offers, he said.
Foreign companies were welcome to team up with local players in bidding, with up to 49 percent direct foreign equity participation allowed, Mah said.
The consortiums preparing to tender for public basic telecommunication services (PBTS) licences in Singapore in 2000 were also invited to bid for the cellular licences, he added.

"The time schedule of the cellular service tender has been synchronised with the PBTS main tender exercise" to allow successful bidders to start basic and mobile telephone services at the same time, he said.
Results of the mobile phone tenders would be announced in mid-1998, giving the winners 18 months to get their networks ready. Mah said.
Singapore has said it will award one or two licences for basic telephone services.

TAS said in a statement that the licences for mobile services would be valid for 17 years from April 1, 2000 to coordinate their expiry with the length of the licence given to MobileOne, Singapore's second service due to start operations on April 1.
MobileOne is a consortium comprising Keppel Corp and Singapore Press Holdings, each holding 35 percent stakes, Britain's Cable & Wireless and Hong Kong Telecommunications, each with 15 percent.
MobileOne will compete against Singapore Telecommunications Ltd.
